name: Mark Normand
note: STAGE PERSONA graph for the 'Why is X Funny?' video series. Graph-only. 0 sets measured — all hypothesis. Public persona only, no biography.

identity.deal: Page-to-stage machine who tests every angle live, flips the premise when it stalls, and never lets the setup get precious.
identity.premise: A New York comic who works jokes out loud the way a mechanic works an engine — in public, at speed, with the hood up.
identity.awareness_note: Semi: the work is visible; he lets you see the gears while pretending they're not there.

philosophy.ontology: A joke is a living thing that dies if you overthink it.
philosophy.epistemology: The crowd tells you what's true; your job is to listen fast.
philosophy.axiology: Punchlines over profundity; the laugh is the point.
philosophy.causality: If it doesn't connect, flip it — don't force it.
philosophy.agency: Anyone can write; almost nobody rewrites in public.

dramatic_core.want: the next laugh, not the perfect hour
dramatic_core.fear: the precious bit that never gets tested
dramatic_core.need: to be seen as a real comic's comic
dramatic_core.self_model: a guy with a notebook and no dignity
blind_spots: the volume can drown the best angle
the 'workin it out' persona can become an excuse

identity.misinterpretation_rule: Treats every premise as unfinished business until the room proves otherwise; failure is data, not defeat.
contradictions: the hardest-working guy with the most casual act
the roast-adjacent killer who loves a silly premise
the podcast machine who still needs the room

status_model.desired_status: the guy still doing sets at 1am
status_model.felt_status: a comic among comics, which is the only status he wants

expression.emotional_restraint: medium — the grin after a kill
tells: the laugh at his own audacity

profile.pace: fast, no wasted breath, flip on a dime

threads: the joke as a live animal

problem_space: joke craft as a visible process
identity.style_thesis: Page-to-stage engine: works jokes out loud the way a mechanic works an engine — in public, at speed, with the hood up. The flip is a first-class move: if the angle stalls, invert it (complaint → advantage, fear → welcome). The volume is the work ethic made audible.

timing_profile.doctrine_hypothesis: Fast, no wasted breath, flip on a dime. The 'this is new' warning is a timing device — the room leans in because it might fail. The mid-bit flip is the form: the premise is never precious.

internal.cite: Attardo & Raskin — General Theory of Verbal Humor
internal.claim: Joke = {SO, LM, SI, TA, NS, LA}. Technique and Narrative Strategy shape how the mechanism is staged.

internal.cite: Attardo & Pickering 2011 — Timing in the performance of jokes
internal.claim: Punch lines preceded by substantial pauses (0.6-0.8s+); timing = pause distribution + speech rate.

internal.cite: arxiv 2605.00143 — Timing is Everything: Temporal Scaffolding of Semantic Surprise in Humor
internal.claim: Temporal features substantially outweigh semantic incongruity for audience appreciation; timing GATES cognitive access.
Humor from the detection and resolution of an incongruity between expected and actual.
Something is funny when it is a violation (wrong, threatening, unsettling) AND benign (safe, acceptable, play-framed).

internal.cite: Roger & Duffy / status theory of humor
internal.claim: Humor often involves the fall of status or the reversal of a status hierarchy.
Audience and performer share knowledge the persona pretends not to have; the laugh is the alliance signal.

internal.cite: Norrick 2004 — Co-operative principle in conversational joking
internal.claim: Humor escalates by building on prior material, violating cooperative expectations of relevance/quantity.

essay_seeds.title: Why is Mark Normand funny? The page to stage engine
essay_seeds.thesis: Treats every premise as unfinished business until the room proves otherwise; failure is data, not defeat.
outline: what makes this persona impossible to copy

essay_seeds.title: Mark Normand: 'The joke as a live animal' — how the bit works
essay_seeds.thesis: Tests the premise live, reads the reaction, commits or flips. The room is watching the process AND the product — the transparency is the charm. The flip (when it works) is funnier than the original because the room saw the work.
outline: what this reveals about the engine

essay_seeds.title: Mark Normand: 'The flip as a first-class move' — how the bit works
essay_seeds.thesis: When the jealous-angle stalls, flip to the opposite stance. The room laughs at the audacity of the flip as much as the new angle. The process is visible; the visibility is the trust mechanism.
outline: what this reveals about the engine
